title: More Choices, Fewer Decisions: Ordinal-Scale Bias in JEV-like Direct-Decision Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.38827v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Direct-decision models turn text into low-latency structured labels and scores, making them attractive for classification and automatic evaluation. Yet reliability requires more than accuracy: a model must also use the ordinal decision scale supplied by the user faithfully. We analyze JEV~1.13 and three open KEV models. Our investigation begins with ANLI, where JEV assigns 38.8\% of all predictions and 51.3\% of errors to Neutral despite 74.95\% accuracy, nearly balanced gold labels, and balanced candidate positions. Across 36 ordinal datasets, final decisions use only 67--76\% of the effective gold support, versus 87--102\% on four nominal tasks. Randomizing candidate order weakens but does not remove this compression. translated_title: 更多选择，更少决策：JEV类直接决策模型中的序数尺度偏差
translated_abstract: 直接决策模型能够将文本转换为低延迟的结构化标签和评分，这使其在分类和自动评估任务中颇具吸引力。然而，可靠性不仅仅在于准确性：模型还必须忠实地使用用户所提供的序数决策尺度。我们分析了JEV 1.13以及三个开源KEV模型。我们的研究从ANLI数据集入手，在该数据集上，尽管JEV达到了74.95%的准确率，且黄金标签和候选位置均近乎均衡，但它仍将38.8%的全部预测以及51.3%的错误分配给了“中立”类别。在36个序数数据集上，模型的最终决策仅使用了67–76%的有效黄金标签支持范围，而在四个名义任务上则达到87–102%。随机化候选顺序能够减弱但无法消除这种压缩现象。在固定评估项与源评分、并平衡黄金标签支持与位置的前提下，我们将决策尺度从K=2逐步细化至K=14；所有模型的尺度利用率均随之下降，在K=14时降至26–75%，尽管候选概率分布仍然保持（摘要原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该研究发现JEV类直接决策模型存在序数尺度偏差，倾向于将决策过度压缩到标签尺度的部分取值上，且随着序数尺度增大利用率进一步下降，即使随机化候选顺序也无法完全消除。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals an ordinal-scale bias in JEV-like direct-decision models, which compress their decisions onto only a subset of the provided label scale, with utilization dropping further as the scale grows and the bias persisting even after randomizing candidate order.
